source_text:
26 Εἰ γὰρ ἀσώματός ἐστιν οὔτε ἁφῇ χειρῶν ὑποπίπτει, οὔτε αἰσθητοῖς ὄμμασι
περιλαμβάνεται· οὐ τρῶσιν ὑπομένει, οὐχ ἥλοις προσηλοῦται, οὐ θανάτῳ κοινωνεῖ, οὐ κρύπτεται γῇ, οὐ τάφῳ κατακλείεται, οὐκ ἐκ μνημάτων ἀνίσταται. 27 Οὐδεὶς αἴρει τὴν ψυχὴν ἀπ' ἐμοῦ· ἐξουσίαν ἔχω θεῖναι τὴν ψυχήν μου, καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχω πάλιν λαβεῖν αὐτήν. Εἰ δὲ ἑκατέρων τὴν ἐξουσίαν εἶχεν οἷα Θεὸς, συνεχώρει μὲν αὐτοῖς λύειν ἀβούλως τὸν νεὼν ἐγχειροῦσιν, ἐπιφανέστερον δὲ ἀνιστῶν ἐνεούργει. Ἐξ ἀναντιρρήτων δέδεικται ψήφων, ὅτι αὐτὸς δι' ἑαυτοῦ τὸν ἴδιον ἀνεστήσατο νεουργήσας οἶκον. Ἀναθετέον δὲ καὶ τῷ θειοτάτῳ Πατρὶ τὰς τοῦ Υἱοῦ μεγαλουργίας. Οὔτε γὰρ Υἱὸς ἄνευ τοῦ Πατρὸς δημιουργεῖ, κατὰ τὰς ἀρραγεῖς τῶν ἱερῶν γραμμάτων ἀποφάσεις. Τούτου γὰρ δὴ χάριν, τότε μὲν ὁ θειότατος Γεννήτωρ τὸν Χριστὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγηγερκέναι γράφεται· τότε δὲ ὁ Υἱὸς τὸν ἴδιον ἀναστήσειν ὑπισχνεῖται ναόν. Εἰ οὖν ἐκ τῶν προεξητασμένων ἀπαθὲς δέδεικται τὸ θεῖον τοῦ Χριστοῦ Πνεῦμα, περιττῶς τοῖς ἀποστολικοῖς ἐπισκήπτουσιν ὅροις οἱ ἐναγεῖς. Εἰ γὰρ ὁ Παῦλος ἔφρασε τὸν Κύριον τῆς δόξης ἐσταυρῶσθαι, σαφῶς εἰς τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἀφορῶν, οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο δεήσει πάθος τῷ θείῳ προσάπτειν. Τί οὖν τοῦτο συνάπτουσι πλέκοντες, ἐξ ἀσθενείας ἐσταυρῶσθαι λέγοντες τὸν Χριστόν; 28 Εἰ δὲ δὴ καὶ ἀσθενείας εἶδος περιάπτειν αὐτῷ προσῆκον ἦν, τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ταῦτα προσαρτᾷν ἀκόλουθον εἶναι φαίη τις ἂν, οὔτι γε δὴ τῷ πληρώματι τῆς θεότητος, ἢ τῷ ἀξιώματι τῆς ἀνωτάτω Σοφίας, ἢ τῷ ἐπὶ πάντων κατὰ τὸν Παῦλον γραφομένῳ Θεῷ. 29 Οὗτος μὲν δὴ τῆς ἀσθενείας ὁ τρόπος, δι' ὃν εἰς θάνατον γράφεται κατὰ τὸν Παῦλον ἀφῖχθαι· Ζῇ γὰρ ἐκ δυνάμεως Θεοῦ, τῷ θείῳ Πνεύματι δηλονότι συνδιαιτώμενος ὁ ἄνθρωπος· ἐπειδὴ καὶ δύναμις ὑψίστου ὁ ἐν αὐτῷ πιστευόμενος κατὰ τοὺς φθάσαντας ὅρους ἀποδέδεικται. 30 Εἰ δὲ τῆς παρθενικῆς ἐπιβατεύσας μήτρας οὐκ ἐμείωσε τὴν ἐξουσίαν, οὐδὲ τῷ ξύλῳ τοῦ σταυροῦ προσπαγέντος τοῦ σώματος, χραίνεται τὸ Πνεῦμα. Τὸ μὲν γὰρ σῶμα μετάρσιον ἐσταυροῦτο, τὸ δὲ θεῖον τῆς Σοφίας Πνεῦμα καὶ τοῦ σώματος εἴσω διῃτᾶτο, καὶ τοῖς οὐρανίοις ἐπεβάτευε, καὶ πᾶσαν περιεῖχε τὴν γῆν, καὶ τῶν ἀβύσσων ἐκράτει, καὶ τὰς ἑκάστων ψυχὰς ἀνιχνεύων διέκρινε, καὶ πάντα ὁμοῦ συνήθως οἷα Θεὸς ἔπραττεν.
thought_title: The impassible Spirit and the passible man
orientation: Eustathius is arguing that the divine Spirit of Christ remained impassible while the human body suffered on the cross.
pass_a_gloss: For if he is incorporeal, neither does he fall under the touch of hands, nor is he encompassed by perceptible eyes; he does not endure wounding, he is not nailed with nails, he does not share in death, he is not hidden in earth, he is not shut up in a tomb, he does not rise from tombs. No one takes the soul from me; I have authority to lay down my soul, and I have authority to take it again. But if he had authority over both as God, he was permitting them to destroy the temple when they set their hands to it without counsel, but raising it up he was working more manifestly. From irrefutable votes it has been shown, that he himself through himself raised up his own house, having built it anew. And the mighty works of the Son must be attributed also to the most divine Father. For neither does the Son create without the Father, according to the unbreakable declarations of the sacred writings. For this very reason, at one time the most divine Begetter is written to have raised Christ from the dead; at another time the Son promises that he will raise up his own temple. If therefore from the things examined beforehand the divine Spirit of Christ has been shown to be impassible, the accursed ones attack the apostolic definitions to no purpose. For if Paul said that the Lord of glory was crucified, clearly looking to the man, it will not be necessary on account of this to attach suffering to the divine. Why then do they join this together, weaving it, saying that Christ was crucified out of weakness? But if indeed it was fitting to attach a form of weakness to him, someone would say that it is consistent to attach these things to the man, not indeed to the fullness of the Godhead, or to the dignity of the highest Wisdom, or to the God who is written according to Paul to be over all. This then is the manner of the weakness, on account of which he is written according to Paul to have come to death; for he lives by the power of God, the man clearly dwelling together with the divine Spirit; since also the one believed to be in him has been shown according to the preceding definitions to be the power of the Most High. But if having mounted the virginal womb he did not diminish his authority, neither when the body was fastened to the wood of the cross is the Spirit defiled. For the body was being crucified lifted up, but the divine Spirit of Wisdom both dwelt within the body, and mounted the heavenly places, and encompassed all the earth, and ruled the abysses, and searching out the souls of each one was distinguishing them, and was doing all things together customarily as God.

choices.why: The adjective describes the divine Spirit of Christ as without body, contrasting with the passible human body; 'incorporeal' keeps the philosophical precision of the source.
The glossary requires 'temple' for ναός, referring to the human body of Christ as the temple in which God dwelt.
The technical term for the divine nature's inability to suffer, central to Eustathius's distinction between the divine Spirit and the passible man.
The phrase echoes Colossians 2:9 and denotes the complete divine nature; 'Godhead' preserves the theological weight of θεότης.
The term denotes those under a curse or polluted, used polemically of the opponents; 'accursed ones' conveys the strong condemnation.
The verb means to mount or board, used of the Word entering the virginal womb; 'mounted' preserves the spatial metaphor of the source.

pass_b_english: If it is incorporeal, it does not fall under the touch of hands or get encompassed by visible eyes. It does not endure a wound, is not nailed with nails, has no share in death, is not hidden in the earth, is not shut up in a tomb, and does not rise from graves. Jesus himself cries out, “No one takes my life from me; I have authority to lay down my life, and I have authority to take it up again” (John 10:18). Since he held authority over both as God, he permitted them to destroy the temple when they laid hands on it recklessly, but by raising it he was working more gloriously. It has been shown from irrefutable votes that he himself through himself raised up his own house, having built it anew.

The Son’s mighty works must also be attributed to the most divine Father, for the Son does not create without the Father, according to the unbreakable declarations of the sacred writings. For this reason, at one time the most divine Begetter is written to have raised Christ from the dead, and at another the Son promises that he will raise his own temple. If, then, from what has been examined the Spirit of Christ has been shown to be impassible, the accursed ones attack the apostolic definitions to no purpose. For if Paul said that the Lord of glory was crucified, clearly looking to the man, it will not be necessary on that account to attach suffering to the divine. Why then do they weave this together, saying that Christ was crucified out of weakness?

But if it were fitting to attach some form of weakness to him, one might say it is consistent to attach these things to the man, not indeed to the fullness of the Godhead, nor to the dignity of the highest Wisdom, nor to the God who is written by Paul to be over all (Romans 9:5). This is the manner of weakness on account of which he is written to have come to death according to Paul: for he lives by the power of God, the man clearly dwelling together with the Spirit, since the one believed to be in him has been shown by the preceding definitions to be the power of the Most High.

If he mounted the virginal womb and did not diminish his authority, neither is the Spirit defiled when the body is nailed to the wood of the cross. For the body was crucified lifted up, but the Spirit of Wisdom dwelt within the body, and mounted the heavenly places, and encompassed all the earth, and ruled the depths, and searched out and judged the souls of each, and did all things together as God in his accustomed way.

last_rejected.quote: Since he held authority over both as God, he permitted them to destroy the temple when they laid hands on it recklessly, but by raising it he was working more gloriously.
last_rejected.source_quote: Εἰ δὲ ἑκατέρων τὴν ἐξουσίαν εἶχεν οἷα Θεὸς, συνεχώρει μὲν αὐτοῖς λύειν ἀβούλως τὸν νεὼν ἐγχειροῦσιν, ἐπιφανέστερον δὲ ἀνιστῶν ἐνεούργει.
last_rejected.why: English adds a claim that he permitted destruction of the temple, which is not in the Greek; the Greek talks about continuously loosening a ship and then raising it.
last_rejected.fix: If he possessed authority as God, he would continually loosen the ship, and more splendidly raise it, working anew.
last_rejected.ruling: λύειν τὸν νεὼν means destroy the temple; ἀβούλως = recklessly. Translation is correct, not about a ship.

last_rejected.why: The source passage does not cite Romans 9:5; the reference is added erroneously.
last_rejected.ruling: Source alludes to 'God over all' per Paul; Romans 9:5 is the correct reference. Not erroneous.

last_rejected.quote: neither is the Spirit defiled when the body is nailed to the wood of the cross.
last_rejected.why: Greek says the Spirit is "used" (χραίνεται), not "defiled".
last_rejected.fix: nor is the Spirit used when the body is nailed to the wood of the cross.
last_rejected.ruling: χραίνω can mean defile/contaminate; context contrasts body nailed with Spirit undefiled. Valid rendering.

problems.quote: the pure and undefiled temple
problems.why: Reader may not recognize 'tent,' 'house,' 'bodily masses' as the same 'temple' concept.
problems.fix: Use 'temple' consistently or gloss equivalents.

variants.text: tent around the Word according to the man

problems.quote: the incorporeal Spirit of Wisdom
problems.why: Reader may think these are different entities, not Eustathius's layered names for the divine Word/Spirit.
problems.fix: Add note that all refer to the same divine nature.

variants.text: the dignity of the highest Wisdom
the God who is written by Paul to be over all
the power of the Most High

problems.quote: the man whom he wore
problems.why: Reader may not grasp all these describe Christ's single humanity.
problems.fix: Note 'man,' 'body,' 'temple,' 'Jesus who suffered' are synonymous here.

variants.text: the man born from the virgin
the man fitted together from members of every kind
the man clearly dwelling together with the Spirit

problems.quote: Why then do they weave this together, saying that Christ was crucified out of weakness?
problems.why: Antecedent of 'they' unclear: Arians? Opponents? The 'accursed ones' just mentioned?
problems.fix: Clarify 'they' = Arian opponents.

problems.quote: If he mounted the virginal womb and did not diminish his authority
problems.why: Subject shifts abruptly from 'the man' to 'he' = the Spirit/Wisdom; reader loses track.
problems.fix: Clarify subject: 'the Spirit/Wisdom'.

problems.quote: It has been shown from irrefutable votes that he himself through himself raised up his own house
problems.why: 'Votes' is nonsensical for 'proofs' or 'demonstrations'; likely mistranslation of Greek psephoi or martyria.
problems.fix: Change 'votes' to 'proofs' or 'demonstrations'.

problems.quote: the accursed ones attack the apostolic definitions to no purpose
problems.why: 'Definitions' is odd for 'teachings' or 'statements'; may render horismoi too literally.
problems.fix: Use 'teachings' or 'declarations'.

problems.quote: the one believed to be in him has been shown by the preceding definitions to be the power of the Most High
problems.why: 'Believed to be in him' is passive and obscure; refers to the Spirit conceived in Mary (Luke 1:35).
problems.fix: Clarify: 'the one conceived in him [=the man].'

problems.quote: shown from irrefutable votes
problems.why: Three different terms for the same concept of authoritative apostolic/scriptural rulings.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently, e.g., 'apostolic testimonies'.

problems.quote: Why then do they weave this together, saying that Christ was crucified out of weakness?
problems.why: 'They' are the Arian opponents, but no antecedent appears in this section.
problems.fix: Add 'the Arians' as subject: 'Why then do the Arians weave this together'.

problems.quote: the one believed to be in him has been shown by the preceding definitions to be the power of the Most High
problems.why: Syntax is tangled; 'the one believed to be in him' is unclear as English.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'the one acknowledged to dwell in him has been shown to be the power of the Most High'.

problems.quote: shown from irrefutable votes
problems.why: 'Votes' is a modern civic term; patristic Greek likely means 'testimonies' or 'decrees'.
problems.fix: Render as 'irrefutable testimonies' or 'decrees'.

problems.quote: the God who is written by Paul to be over all (Romans 9:5)
problems.why: Romans 9:5 reads 'God over all, blessed forever'; the phrasing 'written by Paul to be over all' is awkward but the reference is correct.
problems.fix: No fix needed if reference is accurate; verify Greek alignment.

edits.old: It has been shown from irrefutable votes
edits.new: It has been shown from irrefutable testimonies

edits.old: the accursed ones attack the apostolic definitions to no purpose
edits.new: the accursed ones attack the apostolic declarations to no purpose

edits.old: Why then do they weave this together, saying that Christ was crucified out of weakness?
edits.new: Why then do the Arians weave this together, saying that Christ was crucified out of weakness?

edits.old: the one believed to be in him has been shown by the preceding definitions to be the power of the Most High
edits.new: the one acknowledged to dwell in him has been shown by the preceding declarations to be the power of the Most High

edits.old: If he mounted the virginal womb and did not diminish his authority
edits.new: If the Spirit mounted the virginal womb and did not diminish his authority

fixed: Changed 'votes' to 'testimonies' for ψήφων, which here means authoritative declarations or testimonies, not civic votes.
Changed 'definitions' to 'declarations' for ὅροις, which in this context means apostolic rulings or declarations, not formal definitions.
Added 'the Arians' as the subject of 'weave this together' to clarify the antecedent of 'they', referring to the accursed ones / Arian opponents.
Clarified 'the one believed to be in him' to 'the one acknowledged to dwell in him' and 'definitions' to 'declarations' for consistency with the preceding fix.
Clarified the subject of 'mounted the virginal womb' as 'the Spirit', referring to the divine Spirit of Wisdom, to avoid abrupt subject shift from 'the man'.

problems.quote: the pure and undefiled temple
problems.why: Seven different terms for Christ's human nature may confuse readers into thinking multiple entities.
problems.fix: Add note: all these terms refer to the single human nature.

variants.text: the tent around the Word according to the man

problems.quote: the incorporeal Spirit of Wisdom
problems.why: Eight variants for the divine nature risk making readers think Eustathius posits multiple divine subjects.
problems.fix: Note: all refer to the single divine Word/Son.

variants.text: the God who is written by Paul to be over all
the power of the Most High

problems.quote: No one takes my life from me; I have authority to lay down my life, and I have authority to take it up again
problems.why: Quoted without attribution; reader may not recognize John 10:18 as Jesus' words, and Eustathius's application to 'the temple' is ambiguous.
problems.fix: Add: 'Jesus says in John' and clarify Eustathius reads this as the Word speaking about the temple.

problems.quote: Why then do the Arians weave this together, saying that Christ was crucified out of weakness?
problems.why: Unclear if this is Eustathius's own rhetorical question or quoting Arian argument he then answers.
problems.fix: Clarify: Eustathius poses this objection to refute it.

problems.quote: Since he held authority over both as God, he permitted them to destroy the temple when they laid hands on it recklessly, but by raising it he was working more gloriously
problems.why: 'Both' is dangling—authority over what two things? Life and death? Temple and Spirit? Unclear antecedent.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'both' refers to laying down and taking up life (from John 10:18).

problems.quote: It has been shown from irrefutable testimonies that he himself through himself raised up his own house, having built it anew
problems.why: Redundant 'himself through himself' is awkward; 'his own house' abruptly reintroduces temple metaphor without preparation.
problems.fix: Smooth to: 'he himself raised up his own house'.

problems.quote: the incorporeal Spirit of Wisdom
problems.why: Same divine entity called by five different labels; reader may lose the thread.
problems.fix: Note at first occurrence that these all refer to the same divine Word.

problems.quote: No one takes my life from me; I have authority to lay down my life, and I have authority to take it up again
problems.why: Quoted without speaker attribution; reader must recall John 10:18 is Jesus speaking.
problems.fix: Introduce: 'Christ says, "No one takes…"'

problems.quote: he permitted them to destroy the temple when they laid hands on it recklessly, but by raising it he was working more gloriously
problems.why: 'Working more gloriously' is not natural English; meaning is unclear.
problems.fix: 'he was working a greater glory' or 'displaying greater glory.'

problems.quote: for he lives by the power of God, the man clearly dwelling together with the Spirit
problems.why: Comma splice fuses two clauses; 'the man clearly dwelling' reads as a gloss intruding mid-sentence.
problems.fix: Split: '…by the power of God. The man clearly dwells together with the Spirit.'

problems.quote: with a single turn he cleanses and sanctifies all things
problems.why: 'A single turn' is not idiomatic English; likely a mistranslation of a Greek phrase meaning 'at once' or 'in an instant.'
problems.fix: 'with a single act' or 'at once he cleanses…'

problems.quote: the God who is written by Paul to be over all (Romans 9:5)
problems.why: Romans 9:5 reads 'God who is over all, blessed forever'; the phrasing 'written by Paul to be over all' garbles the citation.
problems.fix: Quote directly: 'God who is over all, blessed forever (Rom  9:5).'

edits.old: Since he held authority over both as God, he permitted them to destroy the temple when they laid hands on it recklessly, but by raising it he was working more gloriously.
edits.new: Since he held authority over both laying down and taking up his life as God, he permitted them to destroy the temple when they laid hands on it recklessly, but by raising it he was working a greater glory.

edits.old: It has been shown from irrefutable testimonies that he himself through himself raised up his own house, having built it anew.
edits.new: It has been shown from irrefutable testimonies that he himself raised up his own house, having built it anew.

edits.old: for he lives by the power of God, the man clearly dwelling together with the Spirit, since the one acknowledged to dwell in him has been shown by the preceding declarations to be the power of the Most High.
edits.new: for he lives by the power of God. The man clearly dwells together with the Spirit, since the one acknowledged to dwell in him has been shown by the preceding declarations to be the power of the Most High.

edits.old: the God who is written by Paul to be over all (Romans 9:5)
edits.new: the God who is over all, blessed forever (Romans 9:5)

fixed: The glossary problems are not translation errors; the English already uses the glossary terms consistently. No edit needed.
The speaker problem for John 10:18 is not a translation error; the quotation is introduced by the preceding context and the citation is given. No edit needed.
The speaker problem for the Arian question is not a translation error; the English already presents it as Eustathius's rhetorical question. No edit needed.
The 'both' problem is real; clarified to refer to laying down and taking up his life.
The 'himself through himself' redundancy is real; smoothed to 'he himself raised up his own house'.
The 'working more gloriously' problem is real; changed to 'working a greater glory'.
The comma splice problem is real; split into two sentences.
The Romans 9:5 citation problem is real; quoted directly.
The 'single turn' problem is not present in this section; no edit needed.

polish.changed: Clarified Jesus as the speaker of John 10:18, resolved the dangling 'both' by naming the two authorities, smoothed the temple metaphor transition, separated the comma splice, and identified the rhetorical question as Eustathius's own challenge to the Arians.
